question: Was this a glacial lake outburst flood?

sideA.label: Early analysts
sideA.text: Initial Wadia Institute-type readings and the tracker framing suggested a possible GLOF.

sideB.label: Later analyses
sideB.text: Satellite and seismic analysis points to a rock-ice avalanche from the Lirung massif turning into a debris flow; EarthSky found no evidence of a classic GLOF.

resolution: Weight of evidence favours rock-ice collapse; a seven-member Nepal panel is still investigating.

question: Did an earthquake trigger the flood?

sideA.label: Early reports
sideA.text: A M4.4 earthquake was reported at 08:37 NPT.

sideB.label: USGS
sideB.text: USGS found no earthquake; the signal (Ms 5.2) was the collapse itself.

resolution: Retracted as a trigger: the seismic signal was the landslide.

question: Did climate change cause the disaster?

sideA.label: BBC/CNN/NPR-cited researchers
sideA.text: Warming probably raised the likelihood by weakening permafrost (Alton Byers).

sideB.label: NYT-cited researchers
sideB.text: Stopped short of attributing this event to climate change.

question: Did Chinese infrastructure or dams in Tibet cause it?

sideB.label: Satellite analyses
sideB.text: Collapse originated near Langtang Lirung on the Nepali side.

resolution: Misinformation; Press Council Nepal ordered 72 users to remove content.

question: Is China's Tibet casualty count accurate?

sideB.label: International Campaign for Tibet
sideB.text: Casualties exceed official figures; up to 300 homes destroyed.

resolution: Unverifiable: foreign press access is supervised.

question: Is information from Tibet being censored?

sideA.label: Chinese foreign ministry
sideA.text: Spokesperson Guo Jiakun warned against smear campaigns and hype; hosted press tour 6 Sep.

sideB.label: Media and ICT
sideB.text: Videos and witness interviews removed; at least 10 people penalised.

resolution: Documented removals; BBC changed wording from 'fully' to 'heavily' censored.

question: Did the early warning system work?

sideA.label: Nepal officials
sideA.text: 679,295 SMS alerts within a minute of the first alerts at 09:15.

sideB.label: Critics
sideB.text: System was tuned to monsoon floods; upstream stations swept away; warning arrived after the flood hit Rasuwa.

sideB.label: Other compilations
sideB.text: 5,285 to 6,145 missing; ~1,000 names added by bookkeeping.

question: Did Nepal reject foreign rescue help?

sideA.label: Nepal government
sideA.text: Declined search teams citing 2015 coordination problems.

sideB.label: Foreign governments
sideB.text: Offered teams quickly (UK, Qatar, Malaysia, Taiwan, others).

resolution: Later admitted experts from India, China, Australia, South Korea.

question: Did the US rescue Americans?

sideA.label: White House
sideA.text: Karoline Leavitt said Washington had rescued a handful of Americans.

resolution: Both can be true; no detailed US figures published.

question: How many workers were at Upper Trishuli 3A?

sideB.label: Other counts
sideB.text: 933 hydropower workers listed across projects in one report.

sideB.label: Later estimate
sideB.text: About 10.6% of hydro and solar output (430.7 MW).
